answer: LINE(2nd) models second-order proximity: two nodes are similar when they share many neighbors, so it emphasizes the similarity of their neighborhood distributions. It uses separate vertex and context embeddings and samples edges directly, with no multi-hop random walks. node2vec instead uses biased second-order random walks, with parameters p and q that interpolate between breadth-first exploration (local, structural-equivalence-like neighborhoods) and depth-first exploration (broader, homophily/community-like neighborhoods). So node2vec offers a tunable mix of structural and homophilous proximity, while LINE(2nd) focuses on shared-neighborhood similarity at a fixed order. On word analogy evaluations, node2vec, which builds on skip-gram over walk sequences, is generally reported to score better overall than LINE(2nd). I could not verify the specific study this question refers to, so the exact scores are uncertain.
